---
title: 'Freeze, fix and record releases'
status: implemented
description: 'Hold every store release during a freeze, ship a hotfix, recover from a halted rollout, record a build you uploaded yourself, and see releases on a calendar.'
---

An app's **Releases** tab shows where each version is on every store track.
It also has the tools for the moments around a release: a freeze when nothing
should change, a hotfix when something must, and a record of uploads made by
hand.

## What you need

- App maintainer, instance admin, or instance owner access to freeze an app,
  lift its freeze, or record a release. Freezing every app takes instance
  admin or owner access.
- Developer access or higher to start a hotfix build.

## Freeze releases

Choose **Freeze releases** on the Releases tab and write why, such as "Sale
weekend". An instance admin or owner can tick **Freeze every app**. Everyone
who opens the app sees the reason, and while the freeze holds:

- builds still run and testers can still install them;
- the runner skips store uploads and says so in the build log;
- promotions, approvals and **Raise**, **Resume**, **Complete**, **Release
  now** and **Resubmit** are refused with the reason;
- scheduled rollout steps wait, and continue after the freeze is lifted;
- **Pause** and **Halt** still work, so a bad release can always be stopped.

Choose **Lift freeze** to end it. The API is `PUT /v1/release-freezes` and
`DELETE /v1/release-freezes/{freeze_id}`.

## Ship a hotfix

On a release that is rolling, paused, halted or out, choose **Ship a
hotfix**. Make a branch from the commit the release was built from, push the
fix to it, and enter the branch. Oore builds it with the same pipeline and
workflow, so it gets a higher version code and the same publish settings.
Release it from its build page when it finishes.

## When a rollout is halted

A halted release stops reaching new users, but a store cannot take an
update back off a phone: the people who already have the version keep it.
The release page says how many that is and offers the ways back:

- **Resume** when the problem turned out to be elsewhere.
- **Ship a hotfix** with the fix.
- **Build the previous version again**: Oore runs the build of the version
  that was out before, which gets a new, higher version code, so the store
  takes it as an update.

## Record a build you uploaded yourself

When a build was uploaded in Play Console or App Store Connect by hand,
choose **I uploaded a build myself**, pick the build and the store, and, for
Google Play, the track. Oore records it as out to everyone on that track, so
the app's releases stay complete. Nothing is sent to the store.

## Release calendar

The **Calendar** under the versions shows each release on the day it
started, a month at a time. Select one to open its page.

## Verify the result

- With a freeze on, start a build of a pipeline that publishes: its log
  says store uploads are frozen and nothing reaches the store.
- After a record, the version shows under **Where each version is**.
